newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury details bank account terms.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury details bank account terms.

text.p: British supermarket J. Sainsbury Plc said its joint-venture with Bank of Scotland, Sainsbury's Bank, would offer an Instant Access account giving 5.75 percent gross annual interest and incentives for customers who transfer balances to its credit cards.

The bank, in which Sainsbury holds 55 percent and Bank of Scotland 45 percent, launched on Wednesday in 244 stores including 115 supermarkets, five Savacentre stores and 124 Homebase do-it-yourself outlets.
Sainsbury said the bank's Visa cards could be used at any outlet displaying the Visa sign and points for its Reward loyalty scheme would be gained for transactions made on the card at other stores.
Customers can also use their cards in 10,000 automatic cash dispensers throughout Britain while Sainsbury's Bank branded machines will open in selected stores.
Sainsbury and Bank of Scotland announced plans for the bank in October 1996 and gained a banking licence earlier this month.

The bank will also offer a Christmas Saver account using standing order payments with interest at 2.5 percent payable in cash or Reward points with an annual bonus of three percent if no funds are withdrawn before the scheme ends.
